summary: A proposal by Jon Postel for a standard Character Generator process that sends character data regardless of input, the opposite of the Discard process in RFC 348. Hosts that choose to could run it, using the Initial Connection Protocol, to help test terminals and connections.

eli5.summary: A machine that keeps writing out letters to you for testing, like a tap you turn on to test your bucket.

subtitle: A standard test service that generates and sends character data

tldr.problem: There was no standard way to test terminals and connections on the network, and each site had to write its own test program.
tldr.mechanism: A standard Character Generator process listens for connections, executes the Initial Connection Protocol, and then continuously sends character data into the network as buffer space becomes available.
tldr.outcome: Hosts can run the Character Generator to provide a standard, simple service for testing their terminals and network connectivity.

today: Chargen is an Internet Standard (STD 62) and has been widely implemented on many systems. It is still used today for testing and diagnostic purposes, though modern systems often prefer more sophisticated testing mechanisms. Most Unix and Linux systems continue to provide chargen for compatibility.

sections.title: The Character Generator Service
sections.content: This RFC proposes a standard Character Generator process (often called Chargen) that any host willing to provide it can implement. The service generates character data without any regard to input, making it the logical opposite of the Discard process described in RFC 348. Many hosts already had existing terminal testing programs (such as TTYTST) that could implement this function adequately.
sections.eli5: A simple service on a computer that just sends characters for you to test if your connection works.

sections.title: How Chargen Works
sections.content:
When a client requests a connection to the Character Generator, the process listens for the incoming connection and executes the Initial Connection Protocol (ICP) as specified in the Current Network Protocols notebook. Upon completion of the ICP, the Character Generator begins to send characters into the network as buffer space is made available.

The process continues sending characters until the client closes the connection. This makes it easy for terminals and programs to test whether they can properly receive data over the network.
sections.eli5: When someone connects to Chargen, it says hello in the network way, then keeps sending letters until they disconnect.

sections.title: Testing and Diagnostics
sections.content: The Chargen service is useful for testing terminal performance, checking network connectivity, validating the correctness of network implementations, and diagnosing problems with connections. Because it is a simple, standard service that generates data in a predictable way, developers and network administrators can use it to verify that their systems can handle incoming data streams correctly.
sections.eli5: Chargen is good for testing if your computer can receive data properly and if your connection to the network is working.
